title: How to Use Fixed Income Products for Stable Retirement Cash Flow
description: Bonds, CDs, and Annuities: Building the 'Safe Floor'.
content:
Retirement requires a shift from 'Total Return' (Growth) to 'Cash Flow' (Income). You can't pay bills with stock appreciation; you pay them with cash. Fixed Income products provide the certainty that stocks lack. By layering Bonds, Certificates of Deposit (CDs), and Annuities, you can build a 'Paycheck' that arrives every month regardless of what the S&P 500 does. This guide explains how to construct a fortress of guaranteed income.

Key Takeaways

  • The 'Bond Ladder': Buying individual bonds that mature every year (e.g., 2026, 2027, 2028) guarantees cash availability. You eliminate interest rate risk by holding to maturity.
  • Annuity Floor: A Single Premium Immediate Annuity (SPIA) acts as a private pension. Covering your essential expenses (Housing/Food) with an annuity allows you to invest the rest of your portfolio aggressively.
  • CDs for Short-Term: Use CD ladders for money needed in 1-5 years. They are FDIC insured and currently offer competitive yields compared to bonds.
  • Asset Location: Bond interest is taxed at ordinary income rates. Always hold these assets in a Traditional IRA or 401(k) to shield the income from annual taxes.

Why It Matters (US Context)

The yield curve dictates strategy. In 2025, short-term rates might be higher than long-term rates. However, 'locking in' long-term rates (even if lower) protects you from future rate cuts. Balance yield with duration.

The Fixed Income Menu

Choose the right tool for the job.

1. US Treasuries (The Gold Standard)

Safety: Risk-Free.
Tax: State Tax Free.
Use: Core safety holding. Buy 'Notes' (2-10 years) for ladders.

2. Investment Grade Corporate Bonds

Safety: High (Companies like Apple/Microsoft).
Yield: Higher than Treasuries.
Use: Yield boosting. Use an ETF like LQD or VCIT for diversification.

3. Fixed Annuities (MYGA)

Safety: Backed by Insurer.
Yield: Often beats CDs. Tax-deferred growth.
Use: The 'CD Replacement'. Lock money for 3-5 years.

Building the Income Machine

  1. Determine the Gap: Expenses - Social Security = $2,000/mo shortfall.
    Goal: Generate $24,000/yr from fixed income.
  2. Ladder Construction: Buy $24,000 of bonds maturing in Year 1, Year 2, Year 3, Year 4, and Year 5. Total Cost: $120,000.
    Result: 5 Years of safety.
  3. The 'Roll': When Year 1 matures, spend it. If stocks are up, sell stocks to buy a new Year 6 bond. If stocks are down, don't buy a bond; just wait. You have 4 years left.
  4. TIPS Allocation: Keep 20% of the bond portfolio in TIPS (Inflation Protected) to hedge against cost-of-living spikes.

Frequently Asked Questions

Why not just buy dividend stocks?

Stocks are volatile. Dividends can be cut. Bonds (held to maturity) are a contract. You know you will get paid. They serve a different purpose (Safety vs Growth).

Can I lose money in bonds?

In a fund (ETF), yes, if rates rise. In an individual bond held to maturity, no. You get your principal back. Retirees often prefer individual bonds for this reason.

What is a MYGA?

Multi-Year Guaranteed Annuity. It's like a CD from an insurance company. It pays a fixed rate for a fixed term. Good for tax deferral.
